<description>
**Problem:** A kernel application whose log callback logs, or destroys a kernel object, hangs. The common way to hit this is a garbage-collected language binding: Python's garbage collector can run finalizers inside the callback, and a finalizer that destroys a chainstate manager flushes and logs (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34775#issuecomment-6278257737, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4030551866). The cause is that the kernel calls log callbacks while holding the logger's mutex, so any logging from inside a callback blocks on a mutex its own thread already holds.

**Solution:** This PR calls log callbacks without holding the mutex. The kernel API is unchanged, including support for multiple logging connections.

This is an alternative to the last commit of #34775, which fixes the same deadlock but only after limiting the process to one logging connection. Fixing the deadlock separately lets it merge without waiting on that API question. If #34775 is going to merge soon with its own fix, this PR can be closed.

Behavior changes for callers:

- Callbacks can run on several threads at the same time, so they must be thread-safe. Entries from different threads arrive in no particular order.
- A callback can log, and can create or destroy kernel objects and other logging connections. Destroying a callback's own connection from inside it aborts instead of hanging.

The change is in `src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp` (about 45 lines) plus header docs and new test_kernel cases, which hang without the fix. Details are in the commit message.
</description>

<commits>
08207f71a6 kernel: Call log callbacks without holding the logger mutex

Release KernelLogger::m_mutex while a log callback runs, so a callback
can log, or destroy kernel objects that log, without deadlocking.
Previously Log() held m_mutex across every callback, so an entry logged
from inside a callback waited for the mutex its own thread held. A
garbage collector running finalizers inside a callback triggers this: a
finalizer that destroys a chainstate manager flushes and logs, and the
process hangs. See
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34775#issuecomment-6278257737
and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4030551866.
Creating or destroying another connection from inside a callback hung
the same way.

Multiple connections and the API are unchanged. Log() walks the list
of callbacks holding m_mutex only to step to the next one, and each
callback has a count of running invocations. Destroying a connection
marks its callback removed so no new invocations start, waits for the
count to reach zero, and then destroys the callback and its user_data
outside m_mutex, so it still waits for invocations on other threads.
The count is only decremented and notified under m_mutex, and destroy
takes m_mutex again before freeing the callback, so Log() never touches
a freed callback. Destroying a connection from inside its own callback
would wait for itself, so it asserts instead.

Behavior change: callbacks can run on several threads at the same time
and must be thread-safe, and entries from different threads have no
global order. The header documents this and which kernel calls are
safe from inside a callback. bitcoin-chainstate and the test logger now
write each line in one call so concurrent lines don't interleave.

New test_kernel cases, which all hang without this change: a callback
that logs and destroys a chainstate manager and context, a callback
that destroys another connection, and destroying a connection while
invocations run on other threads.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5.
</commits>
